info.title: Nizam API — Customer
info.description:
The **Nizam Customer Portal API** is the surface for end buyers — the people who place orders inside a Nizam-powered marketplace. Use this API to manage your profile, view your orders, and track deliveries.

This is one of the [audience-scoped Nizam APIs](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/overview). It shares the wire-level conventions (RFC 9457 errors, cursor pagination) with every other Nizam audience — see the [API conventions reference](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/conventions) for the canonical description. This page covers what's specific to the Customer Portal.

## Audience

This API ships in the **Customer SDK** (`@nizam-os/customer-sdk` on npm). Consumers are individual end buyers using a self-service portal — typically embedded in a merchant's storefront or a Nizam-branded buyer experience.

Tenant-side concerns (organizations, fleet, dispatch) and merchant-side concerns (catalog, fulfillment) are on their respective SDKs and never appear in this surface.

## Authentication

Issued by the **`nizam-customer-portal`** Keycloak client. Authorization Code + PKCE flow.

Every JWT carries:

| Claim | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `azp` | `nizam-customer-portal` — identifies this Portal at the server. |
| `sub` | The customer's UUID. |
| `organization` | The Organization whose marketplace the customer belongs to. May be omitted for cross-tenant customer flows. |
| `resource_access.nizam-customer-portal.roles` | Always contains `customer`. |

## Roles

Single role: `customer`. No further differentiation. Authorization is implicit — every endpoint in this SDK accepts any authenticated customer.

## Surface

The smallest of the Nizam surfaces:

- `/v1/me` — your profile.
- `/v1/lookups/*` — countries, currencies, languages, timezones.
- Customer-specific surface (orders, tracking, addresses) lands as Nizam's commerce surface comes online.

## Privacy

Customer data is scoped to the individual buyer via Postgres Row-Level Security on the `customer_id` session variable. You can only read and modify rows tied to your own `sub` claim — RLS prevents reading another customer's profile or orders even if you forge their id in a path. The platform staff console exists for support actions that legitimately need cross-customer visibility; those actions are audited.

## Status

This SDK is intentionally narrow today. Customer-facing features land alongside the commerce subsystem.

get.description: The active organization's files ordered by `created_at` descending (pass `sort=created_at` for ascending). `kind` / `status` accept comma-separated values; `subject_type` + `subject_id` narrow to the files documenting one business entity. Pagination is bidirectional (`starting_after` / `ending_before`).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by file kind. Comma-separated; values: `profile_picture`, `chat_attachment`, `task_pod_photo`, `import_source`, `import_report`, `signed_document`, `product_image`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle status. Comma-separated; values: `active`, `quarantined`, `deleted`.

parameters.name: subject_type
parameters.description: Filter by the documented entity's type (pairs with `subject_id`).

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: Filter by the documented entity's id (requires `subject_type`).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. Allowed fields: `created_at`. Prefix a field with `-` for descending (e.g. `-created_at`); unknown fields are rejected with `400 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 20, maximum 100. Out-of-range values are silently clamped; the response body's `limit` field reflects what was applied.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor — return the page starting strictly after this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `ending_before`.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor — return the page ending strictly before this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `starting_after`.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user merged with profile claims from their JWT.

JIT-provisions a shadow row on the first call (so a brand-new Keycloak user can hit any
endpoint without an explicit signup step). Records a login (`last_login_at` = the token's
`auth_time`, `login_count` incremented) only when a genuinely new authentication is seen;
repeated calls within the same session don't write.

The `roles` array combines realm roles (flat, e.g. `platform_admin`) with portal-scoped
client roles (prefixed, e.g. `dashboard:dispatcher`). The frontend usually drops the
portal prefix when rendering since it knows its own portal.

post.description: Returns a short-lived ticket to present as `Authorization: Bearer <ticket>` on the STOMP CONNECT frame to `/ws`. Browser clients need this because their Keycloak access token lives in an HTTP-only cookie that JavaScript cannot read; native/mobile clients holding a Keycloak access token may present it directly on CONNECT and skip this call. Mint a fresh ticket per connection attempt — it expires within seconds.

instance.description: URI reference for the specific occurrence (typically the request path).

code.description: Machine-readable identifier. Stable across releases. Snake_case; resource-prefixed for domain errors (e.g., `user.email_already_taken`).

trace_id.description: OpenTelemetry trace id from the request — match to logs for support.

errors.description: Per-field validation errors. Populated only when status=422.

ApiFieldError.description: One field-level entry inside a 422 validation problem.

field.description: Dot-notated JSON path matching the request shape.

UploadInitiation.description: A freshly initiated upload: the session handle, the pre-reserved file id and the presigned part URLs. Resume/complete/cancel go through the generic file-uploads endpoints.

upload_session_id.description: Upload session id — the handle for resume/complete/cancel.

file_id.description: Pre-reserved file id — the id the completed file WILL carry.

part_size_bytes.description: Fixed size of every part except the last.

expires_at.description: Session deadline; the sweep aborts the upload after this.

url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the part's bytes to.

additionalProperties.description: Headers that were signed into the URL; repeat them verbatim.

headers.description: Headers that were signed into the URL; repeat them verbatim.

url_expires_at.description: URL expiry; re-request via resume if it lapses.

CaptureTaskAttemptPhotoRequest.description: Declares a POD photo upload for a task attempt and requests presigned part URLs.

content_type.description: Declared MIME type — POD photos accept image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/heic, image/heif.

size_bytes.description: Exact byte size; verified against storage at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: Client-computed SHA-256 of the content, lowercase hex; re-verified server-side by the pipeline.

sequence.description: Display order within the attempt; defaults to the next free slot.

photo_type.description: Photo category: `proof_of_delivery`, `placement`, `contents`, `damage`, `door`, `signature`, `id_verification`, `barcode`, `site_condition`, `other`. Omit for a free capture.

caption.example: Left at the front door as instructed

taken_at.description: Capture timestamp from the device (EXIF time) — distinct from the upload time, which may lag over flaky mobile connections.

RealtimeTicket.description: A short-lived ticket authorizing a single realtime (STOMP/WebSocket) connection.

ticket.description: The signed ticket. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <ticket>` on the STOMP CONNECT frame to /ws. Opaque to the client; do not parse or store it.

expires_at.description: When the ticket expires (ISO-8601). Connect promptly; mint a fresh ticket for each new connection attempt.

slug.description: Optional URL-safe slug. When omitted, the server derives one from the name.

primary_domain.description: Optional primary email domain. When set, Keycloak attaches it to the new Organization so per-domain IdP discovery works.

business_category.description: Optional self-selected vertical from /v1/lookups/business-categories. Lowercase slug (e.g. 'restaurant', 'third_party_logistics'). Drives downstream personalization.

phone.description: Optional contact phone number in E.164 format (leading +, country code, then digits).

Organization.description: A tenant — a logistics company, 3PL, or LSP.

id.description: Stable UUID owned by Nizam. Pin this value in URLs and external integrations. The matching Keycloak Organization is tracked server-side via a separate keycloak_id bridge and is not exposed over the SDK; do not assume the two ids are equal.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier — used in deep links and admin tooling.

founder_user_id.description: User id of the human who originally created this organization. Immutable for the row's lifetime — does NOT change when ownership is transferred.

owner_user_id.description: User id of the current owner. Receives all admin notifications by default. Mutable; reassigned via ownership transfer. May be null transiently if the owner user has been hard-deleted.

active_organization_id.description: Populated ONLY on the POST /v1/organizations create response — the active organization id Nizam pinned for the founder as part of the same transaction that created the org. Null on every other endpoint (GET, list, membership embeds). Per issue #67 phase 1, the SPA writes its active-org cookie from this field instead of issuing a follow-up PATCH /v1/me/active-organization.

responsible_party.description: Legal entity accountable for this operator's actions (a user id).

user_id.description: Linked user id (when the human has a Nizam login).

CreateOperatorRequest.description: Create a new operator. The kind discriminator selects the variant.

controller_user_id.description: User id of the human controller at the remote console.

Operator.description: A controlling agent — human, autonomous software, teleoperator, or hybrid.

user_id.description: Linked user id (humans with a Nizam login). Null for software agents.

responsible_party_id.description: Legal entity accountable for this operator (required for autonomous/teleoperated).

content_type.description: Declared MIME type — profile pictures accept image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp; re-verified server-side at completion.

size_bytes.description: Exact byte size; verified against storage at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: Client-computed SHA-256 of the content, lowercase hex; re-verified server-side by the pipeline.

MqttToken.description: A short-lived MQTT publish credential for the position ingest broker.

token.description: JWT to present as the MQTT CONNECT password. The CONNECT username must be the operator id embedded in the token's operator_id claim.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires. Re-mint before this elapses to stay connected.

topic.description: The only topic this credential may publish to: nizam/{organizationId}/operators/{operatorId}/location.

Job.description: A long-running, retryable, operator-visible unit of work — bulk imports, exports, backfills, cache rebuilds. The job row is the persistent handle; the executing engine (Temporal workflow or lease worker, declared per kind) reports progress into it. Cancellation is cooperative: already-running work continues until the engine's next checkpoint.

kind.description: What kind of work this job performs; the kind also fixes the executing engine.

requested_by_id.description: User who submitted the job. Null only if that user was since deleted.

source_uri.description: Input handle the job consumes (kind-specific), e.g. an uploaded import file.

report_uri.description: Artifact produced by a completed job (kind-specific), e.g. a result report.

rows_total.description: Total work items, once the engine has sized the work. Null while unknown.

rows_failed.description: Work items that failed so far (monotonic).

error_summary.description: Operator-facing failure reason. Set only when status is `failed`.
error_summary.example: upstream geocoding service returned 503 after 3 retries

workflow_id.description: Temporal workflow id (Temporal-engine kinds only) — cross-reference into the Temporal UI.

run_id.description: Temporal run id of the latest attempt (changes across workflow retries).

attempt_count.description: Engine execution attempts spent so far.

max_attempts.description: Retry budget: a failed job with attempt_count >= max_attempts is dead-lettered.

started_at.description: When the first engine attempt started. Null while pending (and for jobs cancelled before starting).

finished_at.description: When the job reached a terminal status.

role.description: Role the recipient will hold after acceptance.

organization_id.description: Organization the invite confers membership in.

role.description: Role the recipient will hold after acceptance.

expires_at.description: When the invite expires. Recipients must accept before then.

token.description: Bearer secret used to redeem the invite. Returned only on POST /v1/invites; subsequent lookups omit it.

BulkJobSubmission.description: Acknowledgement of a bulk admin action that fanned out one job per work item.

items.description: Created job ids — poll/cancel each via /v1/jobs/{id}.

count.description: Number of jobs created (one per matched service account).

in_kc_only.description: User ids present in the KC member set but not in Nizam.

items.description: User ids present in the KC member set but not in Nizam.

url.description: The URL to GET the bytes from.

FileUploadPart.description: A presigned PUT for one part. Send the raw part bytes; repeat `headers` verbatim; keep the response's `ETag` header for completion.

url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the part's bytes to.

additionalProperties.description: Headers that were signed into the URL — the PUT must repeat them verbatim.

headers.description: Headers that were signed into the URL — the PUT must repeat them verbatim.

url_expires_at.description: When this URL stops working (re-issue via resume).

FileUploadSession.description: A resumable multipart upload in flight. The browser PUTs each part directly to the presigned URL (echoing the part's `headers` verbatim), persists the returned ETags, and completes the session with the full part list. `file_id` is the id the finished file WILL carry — safe to build optimistic UI against.

id.description: Session id — the handle for resume / complete / cancel.

file_id.description: Pre-reserved id of the file this upload will become.

part_size_bytes.description: Nominal part size; every part except the last must be exactly this size.

bytes_uploaded.description: Bytes confirmed so far (client-reported, re-verified at completion).

expires_at.description: Deadline: the session expires and is swept if not completed by then.

InitiateFileUploadRequest.description: Declares an upload and requests presigned part URLs.

kind.description: What the bytes are for the platform — fixes the policy applied to them.

subject_type.description: Type of the business entity this file documents (optional at upload time; can also be attached later).

subject_id.description: Id of the business entity this file documents. Requires subject_type.

filename.description: Original filename; served back via Content-Disposition on download.

content_type.description: Declared MIME type. Must be on the kind's allow-list; re-verified by server-side detection at completion.

size_bytes.description: Exact byte size of the file. Verified against storage at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content as 64 lowercase hex characters (compute with crypto.subtle.digest). Re-verified server-side by the scan pipeline.

File.description: A stored file's metadata: what it is (kind), who uploaded it, integrity (checksum), lifecycle (status + scan verdict + retention), and what business entity it documents (subject). The bytes themselves are served only through short-lived download URLs.

id.description: Stable file id (pre-reserved at upload initiation).

uploader_id.description: Uploading user. Null for system-generated artifacts.

kind.description: What the bytes are for the platform — fixes the size/type/visibility/scan/retention policy applied to this file.

subject_type.description: Type of the business entity this file documents.

subject_id.description: Id of the business entity this file documents.

parent_file_id.description: For derived files (thumbnails): the original this one was rendered from.

original_filename.description: Client-supplied filename, served back via Content-Disposition on download.

declared_content_type.description: MIME type declared by the uploader at initiation.

sniffed_content_type.description: MIME type detected server-side from the bytes (Tika). Null when detection was inconclusive.

size_bytes.description: Object size in bytes, storage-confirmed at completion.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

status.description: Lifecycle: `active` (serving), `quarantined` (malware-positive), `deleted` (bytes purged, row retained under regulatory hold).

visibility.description: Access posture of the bytes, fixed by the kind's policy.

virus_scan_status.description: Malware-scan verdict. Bytes are downloadable only on `clean` or `skipped`.

virus_scanned_at.description: When the scan verdict was produced.

expires_at.description: When this file becomes eligible for the lifecycle sweep (TTL kinds).

retention_until.description: Regulatory hold: the file cannot be deleted before this instant.

limit.description: Page size that produced this response.

expandParam.name: expand[]
expandParam.description: Inline related resources instead of returning id references. Dot-notation for nested (e.g., `order.merchant`). Max depth 4.

fieldsParam.name: fields[<type>]
fieldsParam.description: Sparse fieldsets — JSON:API grammar. The `id` and `object` fields are always returned.

bearerAuth.description: Keycloak-issued JWT bearer token. Use the Dashboard / Merchant / Customer / Carrier portal client for interactive flows, or `nizam-backend` (Client Credentials) for service accounts.
